ai.description: This gecko reaches 50–60 mm SVL. It is pale grey or brown with irregular dark spots and a white venter. Distinctive features include a warty dorsum and a tail with transverse rows of enlarged tubercles.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hemidactylus parvimaculatus* is best distinguished by the presence of 6–8 longitudinal rows of small, weakly keeled tubercles on the dorsum, unlike the smooth-backed *H. frenatus*.
ai.habitat: *Hemidactylus parvimaculatus* typically inhabits tropical deciduous forests and human-modified landscapes, ranging from sea level up to approximately 1,500 meters in elevation.
ai.behavior: *Hemidactylus parvimaculatus* is primarily nocturnal, actively hunting insects and small invertebrates on vertical surfaces like walls and tree trunks after sunset.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hemidactylus parvimaculatus* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of two hard-shelled eggs. Breeding occurs throughout the year, peaking during the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hemidactylus parvimaculatus* is found across southern India and Sri Lanka, primarily inhabiting low-to-mid elevation tropical forests and human-modified landscapes.
